note: Input packet data is assigned as the parsing buffer for the mDNS message.
Allocates space for 2 answer resource structs in m->_packet, advancing m->_len to 112.
Reads attacker-controlled rdlength (9884) from input for the first TXT record.

m->_len advances to 9999 (112+3+9884). The check uses > instead of >= against MAX_PACKET_LEN, allowing m->_len to reach exactly MAX_PACKET_LEN-1 which causes the subsequent label write to overflow by 1 byte.
For the second record, name is set to m->_packet + 9999, one byte before the end of the buffer.
Bounds check uses > instead of >=. With name at offset 9999 and labelLen=1, 9999+1=10000 is NOT > 10000, so the check passes.
Writes '.' at m->_packet[10000], which is 1 byte past the end of the stack-allocated _packet buffer (MAX_PACKET_LEN=10000). This is the stack-buffer-overflow WRITE 1.
